title: Energy Kiosk
description: In 2009, e.quinox launched its first pilot Energy Kiosk in Rwanda, marking the organisation's very first expedition on the ground. The trip was an opportunity to test a new technical solution and explore how a sustainable business model could bring reliable electricity to rural communities.
description2: The kiosk was monitored remotely through a custom data-logging system and maintained by Rwandan partners, ensuring it could keep running long after the team returned to London. This pioneering project gave e.quinox its first real-world proof of concept and a platform to grow future initiatives.
outcomes: First e.quinox installation on the ground
Remote monitoring via a custom data-logging system
Community ownership and maintenance model established

title: Home Lighting
imageAlt: Portable battery boxes distributed in Rwandan homes - 2013
description: In 2013, e.quinox returned to Rwanda to expand their work through a new home lighting initiative. The team worked with local communities to deliver portable battery boxes, giving households access to reliable light and power for the first time.
description2: Alongside this, they trained and collaborated with local entrepreneurs to manufacture and distribute the systems. The expedition strengthened e.quinox's approach of combining engineering solutions with community-led development, creating a foundation for future projects.
outcomes: Portable battery boxes deployed to homes
Local entrepreneurs trained to manufacture and distribute
Community-led distribution network established

title: Rainwater Recon
imageAlt: 2024 expedition installing rainwater harvesting at a rural home in Rwanda
description: In 2024, a team went to Rwanda to introduce an initiative aiming to improve the quality and quantity of water access. This project brought rainwater harvesting to homes - offering a scalable, accessible and transportable solution to improve water access across rural Rwanda.
description2: They received guidance from Rwanda's Ministry of Infrastructure, as well as the opportunity to collaborate with the Dean of Engineering at the University of Rwanda. This allowed e.quinox to receive invaluable feedback that will influence their design and engineering choices going forward.
outcomes: First water-access project for e.quinox
Partnership with Rwanda's Ministry of Infrastructure
Collaboration with the University of Rwanda

title: Project Amazi
imageAlt: Project Amazi - modular 700 L rainwater harvester deployed at a home in Minazi, Gakenke District, Rwanda.
description: Project Amazi is e.quinox's 2026 initiative: a deployable, modular rainwater harvester for rural Rwandan households. Each unit is 700 L and connects in parallel with the next - families scale the system as their savings, or their rainfall, allow. Four years of research in Gakenke District, led by Riccardo Casonato (Imperial College London), have produced a business case that is now in pilot in Minazi Sector.
description2: At 3.2× cheaper to install and 3.8× cheaper to run than a WASAC communal pumped tap, Amazi meets more than 40% of intermediate water-access demand for nine months of every year in all five Rwandan provinces - even at a conservative 50% rain-capture rate. The system is entirely hand-carryable (motos + public transport), cutting delivery costs by more than 90%, and is built from components manufactured or imported into Rwanda. The first version has just been deployed in Minazi, and MININFRA has agreed to evaluate the business case for national policy alignment.
outcomes: First 700 L modular harvester deployed in Minazi Sector
Water-quality testing confirms fitness for all non-potable uses
3.2× cheaper install, 3.8× cheaper OPEX vs WASAC communal tap
>40% of intermediate water-access demand met, 9 months/year, all provinces
Business case delivered to MININFRA for policy review
Hand-carryable supply chain - 90%+ reduction in delivery cost

title: Truckle
imageAlt: Truckle prototype build - earlier e.quinox project, archived.
description: Truckle was an earlier prototyping effort by an e.quinox committee, exploring portable engineered solutions for off-grid Rwandan households. The build process, captured here, laid groundwork for many of the deployable-design instincts that resurface in Project Amazi.
description2: Like every e.quinox project, Truckle was prototyped at Imperial, taken on expedition for field-testing, and ultimately handed over to its Rwandan stewards. Filed in the archive as part of the chapter that runs from 2009 to today.
outcomes: Prototype designed, built and field-tested by an Imperial student team
Lessons folded into later expeditions
Documented for future committees

title: Mushroom Farming Research
imageAlt: Mushroom farming research - earlier e.quinox project, archived.
description: An earlier e.quinox research strand investigating mushroom farming as a complement to the energy and water work in rural Rwanda - looking at protein, income generation, and nutrient cycling potential at the household scale.
description2: The research informed the committee's broader thinking on how engineered infrastructure dovetails with agricultural opportunity. Filed in the archive as part of the wider mission to deliver tools communities use to uplift themselves.
outcomes: Field study and feasibility assessment completed
Insights on income and nutrition pathways recorded
Documented for future committees and partners
